title: THE FOUR OLDS audio play — a09_grave

lines.sfx: Wind moves over the cemetery grass and hums in the chain-link fence.
Cricket comes up a row of stones on the dry grass with a fist of zinnias, and his boots stop at one.
Dutch comes a step behind him and stops off at the corner of the plot.
Cricket goes down on one knee and brushes the grass clippings off the top of the stone.

lines.text: Peg had these all down the fence line. Orange ones, mostly.

lines.sfx: He works the stems down into a canning jar and stands it at the foot of the stone, and the glass knocks once on the granite.

lines.text: (off) When'd she start in on Marwani.
First time the man was ever on the television. Watched him maybe a minute and said he was selling something. Never trusted him a day after. And you know she had a kind word for about everybody.
(off) Before he ever had the county, then.
Long before. Made her mind up right there in the front room and never went back on it.

lines.sfx: Dutch doesn't say anything, and the wind fills the quiet a while.
Cricket presses the jar down into the grass until it stands on its own.
